### OSI model (text)  {.smaller}

<table>
<tr><td>7</td><td>application</td><td>what requests/etc.</td></tr>
<tr><td>6</td><td>presentation</td><td>format of data</td></tr>
<tr><td>5</td><td>session</td><td>coordinate multiple streams</td></tr>
<tr><td>4</td><td>transport</td><td>streams of data</td></tr>
<tr><td>3</td><td>network</td><td>message to correct network</td></tr>
<tr><td>2</td><td>data link</td><td rowspan="2">message to correct machine<br>message into bits/symbols</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>1</td><td>physical</td><td>transmit bits/symbols on medium</td></tr>
</table>
 

* internet: usually combines layers 7/6/5


### OSI model  {.smaller}


* standardized by ISO (International Standards Organization) and ITU (International Telecommunications Union)
* full set of protocols... 

   * file transfer, message sending, directory lookups ...

* that were often implemented and sometimes used...
* but mostly lost out to IETF-standardized Internet protocols 

   * Internet Engineering Task Force



### OSI influence (1) 


* term ‘layer 7’, ‘layer 4’, ‘layer 3’, etc. almost always refer to OSI model
* ...even though most of Internet does not follow it 

   * early Internet protocols predate OSI



### OSI influence (2)  {.smaller}


* are a lot of Internet protocols influenced by OSI protocols
* OSI's DAP (directory access protocol)  

   * adapted into IETF's LDAP (lightweight directory access protocol)

* OSI presentation layer ASN.1 used in... 

   * telephony (between telephone companies)
   * inter-bank messaging
   * lots of cryptography-related protocols
   * ...

* OSI's routing protocol IS-IS still common in large Internet-connected networks 

   * (adapted to work alongside IETF protocols)



### Internet layers  {.smaller}

<table>
<tr><td>OSI layer</td><td>name</td><td>examples</td><td>purpose</td></tr>
<tr><td>7</td><td>application</td><td>HTTP, SSH,<br> SMTP DNS, ...</td><td>application-defined meanings</td></tr>
<tr><td>4</td><td>transport</td><td>TCP, UDP, ...</td><td>reach correct program, reliablity/streams</td></tr>
<tr><td>3</td><td>network</td><td>IPv4, IPv6, ...</td><td>reach correct machine (across networks)</td></tr>
<tr><td>2</td><td>link</td><td>Ethernet, Wi-Fi, ...</td><td>coordinate shared wire/radio</td></tr>
<tr><td>1</td><td>physical</td><td>...</td><td>encode bits for wire/radio</td></tr>
</table>


### Internet protocols and layers (non-exhaustive) 



::: {.r-stack .my-full}
![](/intro/texfig/layer-model-internet-protocols-and-layers-non-exhaus.figure-1.svg){.fragment .fade-out fragment-index=2 fig-alt="Diagram of internet protocols organization into layers: At top, the application layer (OSI layer 7) includes FTP and HTTP built on TCP, and DNS and TFTP in application layer built on UDP. Below them, the transport layer (OSI layer 4) includes TCP and UDP, both built on IP. Then, the network layer (OSI layer 3) includes only IP. Below that in the data link layer (OSI layer 2) are a variety of data link protocols (not named here) that IP can be built on."}

![](/intro/texfig/layer-model-internet-protocols-and-layers-non-exhaus.figure-2.svg){.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=2 fig-alt="In these protocols, IP is exceptionally in that it is a 'narrow waist' &mdash; it is a single protocol supporting a variety of protocols in the layers above and below."}


:::
